info.title: Arker Public VM API
info.description: Public VM and control-plane API contract. Every supported deployment exposes the same wire shapes. Features that are unavailable in a selected region or provider return an `ErrorResponse` with `code: "unsupported_operation"`.

tags.name: Policies
tags.description: Control inbound and outbound VM network access.

tags.name: Sync
tags.description: Read and write files in a VM.

tags.description: Create shared filesystems and mount them into VMs.

200.description: Service is ready to accept public API traffic.

503.description: Service is live but not currently ready to accept public API traffic.

get.description: Public health and readiness probe. Returns service status and server time.
Public placement catalog. Each item supplies the provider, region, and regional endpoint. Every listed placement accepts fork, run, and sync requests. Unavailable placements are omitted.
Returns the organization associated with the authenticated API key or session.

post.description: Create a new VM from an existing VM ID, an organization-scoped VM name, an OCI image, or a Dockerfile. For named sources, the scope can be the caller organization or `ArkerHQ`.

get.description: List VMs visible to the authenticated caller, optionally filtered by region, provider, owner, visibility, lifecycle state, platform, or creation time. All filters compose with AND semantics.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: Narrow to a customer-facing service region (e.g. `us-west`). When omitted, the response aggregates across every configured service region.

parameters.name: provider
parameters.description: Narrow results to a provider.

parameters.name: org_id
parameters.description: List public VMs owned by this organization. Use `ArkerHQ` with `public=true` for the public template catalog.

parameters.name: public
parameters.description: Filter by public visibility. Use with `org_id=ArkerHQ` to list the public template catalog.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Filter by VM lifecycle state.

parameters.name: platform
parameters.description: Match a concrete VM platform ID exactly. A public template matches when any compatible_platforms entry has this ID.

parameters.name: created_after
parameters.description: Include VMs created at or after this RFC 3339 timestamp. An explicit UTC offset is required.

parameters.name: created_before
parameters.description: Include VMs created before this RFC 3339 timestamp. An explicit UTC offset is required.

200.description: VMs visible to the authenticated caller.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Unix epoch seconds; include runs at or after this time.

parameters.name: until
parameters.description: Unix epoch seconds; include runs before this time.

parameters.name: vm
parameters.description: Single VM ID filter.

parameters.name: vms
parameters.description: Comma-separated VM ID filter.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: Region filter.

parameters.name: provider
parameters.description: Provider filter.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Free-text search across run metadata.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of rows to return. The maximum is 200 normally and 20,000 when `lite=true`.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Number of rows to skip.

parameters.name: lite
parameters.description: When true, omit large input and output previews where supported.

parameters.name: runtime
parameters.description: Runtime filter.

parameters.name: endpoint

parameters.name: actions

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Comma-separated status class filter.

parameters.name: status_min
parameters.description: Minimum HTTP/status code filter.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort column.

parameters.name: dir

200.description: Runs visible to the authenticated caller across VMs, providers, and regions.

get.description: Control-plane listing of run activity visible to the authenticated caller across VMs, providers, and regions.
Return one VM visible to the authenticated caller.

delete.description: Delete a VM owned by the authenticated caller.

patch.description: Update a VM's resources, SSH keys, or network policy.

get.description: Return the VM's network policy together with its derived inbound exposure and enforcement metadata. The base application hostname is nullable; non-default ports use `<vm>-<port>.<provider>-<region>.arker.app`.

200.description: The VM's policy document (empty when none is set), plus its derived inbound exposure metadata.

put.description: Replace the complete network policy of a mutable VM owned by the authenticated caller and apply it to the running VM. Public base VMs are immutable.

200.description: Stored policy, plus request-level enforcement domains and any non-fatal notices.
The run finished inside the synchronous window. `state` is terminal and `exit_code` is the command's real status.

202.description: Accepted — the run is still executing. The body carries `run_id` and `state: "running"`, not output; poll `GET /v1/vms/{id}/runs/{run_id}` for the result. Returned for `time_to_background: 0` and whenever the command outstays `time_to_background`. A 2xx here means the request was accepted, not that the work is done.

post.description: Run a command. Set `time_to_background` to `0` to return a pollable run immediately after successful dispatch. A positive value bounds the synchronous wait, and omission uses the default window. A run that is still executing when the response is sent returns **202 Accepted** with a `run_id`; only a run that finished returns 200. Control requests do not accept `time_to_background`. `timeout` is the separate execution and kill bound.

get.description: List recorded runs for one VM, with optional lifecycle and time filters.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Return only runs in this lifecycle state.

parameters.name: started_after
parameters.description: Return runs started at or after this RFC 3339 timestamp.

parameters.name: started_before
parameters.description: Return runs started at or before this RFC 3339 timestamp.

parameters.name: completed_after
parameters.description: Return runs completed at or after this RFC 3339 timestamp.

get.description: Return one recorded run, including its current state and available output.

delete.description: Request cancellation of an in-flight run.

get.description: List persistent command sessions for one VM.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Return only sessions in this lifecycle state.

post.description: Create a persistent command session in a VM.

patch.summary: Update a session (resize PTY / set timeout)
patch.description: Resize the session's PTY (cols/rows) and/or update its idle timeout. Resize is delivered to a LIVE attached PTY in-band; if the PTY is detached, it is applied directly to the session's runtime; if no PTY has ever attached, the call is accepted as a no-op. REST equivalent of the WebSocket {"type":"resize"} control frame — usable from any client, attached or not.

delete.description: Close and remove a persistent VM session.

parameters.name: cols
parameters.description: Initial terminal width in columns.

parameters.name: rows
parameters.description: Initial terminal height in rows.

parameters.name: command
parameters.description: Single executable path to launch (no shell-splitting). Defaults to the login shell.

parameters.name: persist
parameters.description: When true (default), disconnecting keeps the shell running so the same session_id can reconnect to it and receive recent scrollback. When false, the shell is terminated on disconnect. A kill control message or the configured idle TTL terminates a persistent shell.

parameters.name: cancel_ttl_secs
parameters.description: Destroy the PTY after this many seconds without terminal input or output. Omit or set to zero to disable this PTY-specific idle limit.

parameters.name: ticket
parameters.description: Browser auth: a short-lived ticket from POST .../pty-ticket, used in place of the Authorization header (which a browser WebSocket cannot set).

get.description: Upgrades to a WebSocket carrying an interactive pseudo-terminal in the VM, reusing the same interactive terminal as SSH. Authenticate with a bearer API key or, for browser clients, a short-lived PTY ticket. Reopening the same `session_id` reconnects to a persistent shell and replays recent scrollback. Binary server frames contain raw terminal output; binary client frames contain stdin bytes. Text client frames accept JSON controls for `resize`, `kill`, and `ping`. Closing the socket detaches a persistent shell or destroys a non-persistent shell; `kill` always destroys it. The service enforces attachment limits and closes oversized or idle connections.

101.description: Switching Protocols — the WebSocket PTY stream is established.

post.description: Returns a short-lived, multi-use credential for opening the PTY WebSocket from a browser, which cannot set an Authorization header. The bearer-authenticated caller must own the VM. Pass the returned credential as the `ticket` query parameter on the PTY WebSocket URL.

Create a persistent sync: ensure a Filesystem exists (creating
one if requested) and bind-mount it into this VM at `path`.
Bidirectional by virtue of being a mount — there is no separate
sync-direction parameter. Returns `ErrorResponse` code
`conflict` if a sync already exists at `path`.

get.description: List persistent filesystem mounts for one VM, optionally filtered by filesystem.

parameters.name: filesystem_id
parameters.description: Return only mounts for this filesystem.

delete.description: Remove a persistent filesystem mount from a VM.

200.description: Read or write result, matching the request op.

post.description:
Read or write files in the VM filesystem. Op-discriminated:
`{op:"read",path}` reads a file (inline content for small files, a
presigned GET URL for large ones); `{op:"write",writes:[...]}` writes,
each entry an inline chunk or a presigned-upload step. Binding a
filesystem into the VM is the separate `/v1/vms/{id}/syncs` resource.

post.summary: Stream a file or archive into the VM

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Absolute destination path. With `extract` set this is the destination DIRECTORY.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: Exact byte length of the streamed body. The request fails if the stream does not match.

parameters.name: sha256
parameters.description: Optional checksum, verified on the write that completes the file.

parameters.name: extract
parameters.description: Treat the body as a tar archive and extract it into `path` server-side, so a whole directory syncs in one request. Use `tar` for already-compressed data and `tar.gz` when compression reduces the upload size.

post.description: Stream raw bytes directly into the VM as they arrive, avoiding an intermediate copy. With `extract` set, the body is a tar archive and `path` is the destination directory: the archive is unpacked into `path`, so a whole directory syncs in a single request.

get.description: List shared filesystems visible to the authenticated caller.

parameters.name: name_prefix
parameters.description: Return only filesystems whose names begin with this value.

post.description: Create a shared filesystem owned by the authenticated caller's organization.

get.description: Return one shared filesystem visible to the authenticated caller.

delete.description: Delete a shared filesystem after all VM mounts have been removed.

200.description: Delete result. The filesystem must not be mounted by any VM (no remaining `Sync` referencing it).

PtyTicket.name: ticket
PtyTicket.description: Short-lived browser credential created by the PTY ticket endpoint.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Makes run submission safely retryable. Reusing a key with the same request returns the original result; reusing it with a different request returns a conflict.

VmId.name: id
VmId.description: VM identifier: a VM id, or a name. Names resolve in the public base-VM registry first (e.g. ubuntu-full), then among the calling organization's own named VMs. Names never have the shape of a VM id.

Cursor.name: cursor
Cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor returned by the previous page's `next_cursor`.

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description: Maximum items per page. Service caps may apply.

RetryAfter.description: Delay in seconds before retrying a transiently unavailable request.

PaymentRequired.description: The organization must complete billing setup or payment before starting new compute.

UnsupportedOperation.description: The request is valid, but the requested operation or option is unavailable in the selected region or provider.

error.message: background runs are unavailable in the selected region

status.description: Readiness status. `ok` means the service is ready; other values may be returned with HTTP 503.

timestamp.description: Server time when the health response was generated.

org_name.description: Display name of the authenticated organization.

provider.description: Infrastructure provider identifier for the placement.

endpoint.description: Base URL for this placement's regional API.

regions.description: Provider and region placements that accept public API requests.

ErrorCode.description: Stable machine-readable error code. `unsupported_operation` means the requested optional feature is unavailable in the selected region or provider. `payment_required` means billing setup or payment is required before new compute can start. `rate_limited` means the organization exceeded its request rate. `upstream_rate_limited` means a third-party service the request directed Arker to contact — a registry named by `image`, today — rate limited Arker while acting on the caller's behalf; unlike `rate_limited`, the limit is not Arker's and not the organization's request rate, so the remedy is with that service (authenticate, or pull less from it); `message` carries the upstream's own words, including which host refused. `budget_exceeded` means the organization reached its monthly spending limit. `concurrency_limit_exceeded` means the organization reached a global concurrent compute-resource limit. `regional_concurrency_limit_exceeded` means the organization reached a concurrent compute-resource limit in the selected region. `resource_pressure` means the serving infrastructure is temporarily at capacity. `capacity_unavailable` means no worker can currently serve the requested platform and one is being brought up; unlike `unavailable`, which signals a fault, this is an expected transient state and the accompanying `retry_after` says when to try again.

message.description: Human-readable, client-safe error message. For `code: "internal"`, this is intentionally generic.

timestamp.description: Server time when the error response was generated.

retry_after.description: Suggested retry delay in seconds. Present on retryable responses and mirrored by the Retry-After header.

operation.description: Operation that failed, when the service can identify it safely.

runtime.description: Runtime involved in the failure, when safe to expose.

provider.description: Public provider involved in the failure, when safe to expose.

retryable.description: Whether clients should retry the operation.

scope.description: Quota scope that denied the operation.

region.description: Region whose quota denied the operation.

requested_increment.description: Positive allocation added by the operation.

action.description: Stable Console action for resolving the denial.

VmState.description: Unified lifecycle state for a VM or a Session. `idle` means no command is currently executing; `running` means a command is in flight.

RunState.description: Lifecycle state for a run. `pending` means the run was accepted but has not started yet because an earlier run on the same session is still in flight; it is not terminal, and a client should keep polling. `running` means the command is in progress. `completed` means the command finished; `exit_code` reports its result. `failed` means the service could not start or finish the command, with a client-safe explanation in `fail_reason`. `cancelled` means the client cancelled the run.

Provider.description: Infrastructure provider currently hosting the resource.

PolicyWriteRequest.description: A complete replacement for a VM's network policy. Rules are evaluated in order, and the first matching rule determines the result. An empty rule list allows all outbound traffic and permits authenticated inbound access to any guest port.

policies.description: Ordered network policy rules. An empty list allows all outbound traffic and permits inbound traffic to any guest port after Arker authentication. In a non-empty document, unmatched outbound traffic is denied. If no inbound rules are present, inbound access keeps the authenticated default; explicit inbound allow rules restrict exposure to their listed ports.

secrets.description: Named secret values referenced by `${secret:NAME}` in rewrite actions. Values are encrypted at rest and masked in subsequent policy responses.

hostname.description: Server-derived; accepted and ignored on write so a client can PUT back a document it read. Nullable base `.app` hostname for inbound services. The bare hostname selects guest port 8080. For another port, insert `-<port>` before the first dot: `<vm>-<port>.<provider>-<region>.arker.app`. Clients must not require this field to be present.

mitm_domains.description: Server-derived; accepted and ignored on write so a client can PUT back a document it read.

warnings.description: Server-derived; accepted and ignored on write so a client can PUT back a document it read.

PolicyDoc.description: A VM's current network policy and its derived inbound exposure metadata.

policies.description: Ordered network policy rules. An empty list allows all outbound traffic and permits inbound traffic to any guest port after Arker authentication. In a non-empty document, unmatched outbound traffic is denied. If no inbound rules are present, inbound access keeps the authenticated default; explicit inbound allow rules restrict exposure to their listed ports.

secrets.description: Named secrets referenced by `${secret:NAME}` in rewrite actions. Stored values are represented as `***`; supply the original value when replacing a policy that uses it.

hostname.description: Nullable base `.app` hostname for inbound services. The bare hostname selects guest port 8080. For another port, insert `-<port>` before the first dot: `<vm>-<port>.<provider>-<region>.arker.app`. Clients must not require this field to be present.

mitm_domains.description: Domains whose matching traffic is evaluated by the request-level policy engine.

PolicyEntry.description: One policy rule. `match` AND's its present fields (absent ⇒ catch-all).

type.description: Traffic direction: `outbound` controls connections initiated by the VM; `inbound` exposes a guest port. Unknown values are rejected.

auth.description: Authentication for an inbound rule that exposes a port — `allow`, or a scaling-only action. `open` exposes the port publicly; `arker` requires `Authorization: Bearer $ARKER_API_KEY` from the VM owner's organization before forwarding to the guest. The default is `arker`. This field is invalid on deny and outbound rules. All port-exposing inbound rules in one document must use the same authentication mode. Inbound port matches must use individual ports rather than ranges.

PolicyMatch.description: Match criteria: present fields are combined with AND; list items are combined with OR. `ips` and `hosts` are mutually exclusive, and inbound rules cannot use `hosts`. Port, IP, and host rules operate at the connection layer. Method, path, header, and body rules operate at the request layer.

ports.description: Single ports and/or inclusive [start, end] ranges, e.g. [80, 443, [1000, 2000]]. Empty/absent = any port. Inbound allow rules require one or more individual ports and reject ranges.

ips.description: IPs or CIDRs. Outbound rules match destination IPs; inbound rules match the caller source IP.

hosts.description: Label-boundary suffix match on the request host: `github.com` matches `api.github.com`, not `evilgithub.com`.

methods.description: HTTP methods matched by this rule.

headers.description: Header name → any-of values (names AND'd, a name's values OR'd).

body_contains.description: Substrings that must appear in the request body.

oneOf.description: The object action: at least one of `rewrite` / `gate` / `scaling` must be present. The request is forwarded upstream (applying `rewrite` if present); a `gate` blocks it until an outbound HTTP check allows it; a `scaling` key lets the platform suspend the machine while it waits on the response. The three compose freely on one action.

PolicyAction.description: allow / deny, or an object with any combination of `rewrite`, `gate`, and `scaling` (at least one).

ScalingAction.description: Auto-scaling behavior for matched traffic. On an `outbound` rule it brackets the time the VM is blocked awaiting an upstream response; on an `inbound` rule it brackets the time the VM is idle between requests (scale to zero). Outbound rules may be narrowed by L7 criteria (`methods`/`paths`/`headers`/`body_contains`), for example to suspend only on `POST /v1/messages`, and compose with `rewrite` / `gate` siblings. For outbound, prefer a `match.hosts` scope: a host-less scaling rule matches every flow it can see, which breaks certificate-pinning clients. Where each is enforced differs and explains the asymmetry: an `outbound` rule runs on the MITM (TLS-terminating) data path, which is why it can match L7 fields and carry `rewrite`/`gate` siblings; an `inbound` rule is enforced host-side on the plaintext request the worker already holds, so no MITM is involved and no TLS is terminated.

suspend.description: Suspend the VM (snapshot and free CPU/RAM). On an `outbound` rule: while a matched upstream request is blocked, resuming when the response arrives. On an `inbound` rule: once a matched request's response has been fully delivered and nothing else is in flight, so the next matched request wakes it again. The suspended window remains part of the VM's Running interval until the VM is paused or stopped. On an `outbound` rule, matched responses are delivered only once the upstream response is COMPLETE: a suspended VM has no running guest to receive bytes, so the proxy holds the whole body and hands it over at the end. Total latency is unchanged, but a response whose fragments are individually usable — an SSE token stream, for example — stops arriving incrementally, so a client rendering tokens as they arrive will see nothing until the response finishes. Enabling this is a deliberate trade of incremental delivery for the memory saving.

wake.description: Whether a matched inbound request may wake a suspended VM. Omit this field to allow waking. Set it to `false` so a request that would need to start the VM fails with `503 vm_suspended`; requests received while the VM is running are served normally. This field is not valid on outbound rules.

Rewrite.description: Mutate-and-forward. Host/path/header/body values support request-time `$`-token interpolation: `$domain`, `$path`, `$method`, `$vm_id`, `$body` (the request body as received, also `${…}`-braced), and `$$` for a literal `$`. Unknown/unresolved tokens pass through unchanged.

remove_headers.description: Request header names to remove before forwarding.

body.description: Replace the request body entirely with this (interpolated) value; `$body` re-injects the original body. Absent = body forwarded unchanged.

Gate.description: `action.gate` performs an outbound HTTP authorization check before opening the VM's matching connection. A response status in `allow_on_status` permits the connection and applies any sibling `rewrite`; any other status denies it. Timeouts and connection failures follow `deny_on_timeout`, which defaults to deny. `path`, header values, and string leaves of `body` support `$` substitution with the documented request variables. `host` is not substituted. Injected JSON values are escaped, and gate requests reject private, link-local, and internal destinations.

host.description: Target endpoint INCLUDING scheme, e.g. https://authz.example.com. Not interpolated.

headers.description: Request headers with interpolated values. Stored credentials are encrypted at rest and masked in policy responses.

body.description: JSON request body; string leaves are interpolated and JSON-escaped. Absent = no body.

allow_on_status.description: HTTP status codes that mean ALLOW. Any other status denies. Must be non-empty.

deny_on_timeout.description: Verdict on timeout / connection failure: true = deny (fail-closed, default), false = allow (fail-open).

timeout_ms.description: Max wall-clock for the gate call before it is abandoned (then deny_on_timeout applies). Default ~30000.

source_vm_id.description: Global VM identifier. Org is inferred from the row.

source_vm_name.description: VM name within the caller organization or `ArkerHQ`. Omit the organization scope to search the caller first and then `ArkerHQ`.

image.description: OCI image reference to fork from — for example `ubuntu:24.04`, `ghcr.io/org/image:v1`, or `image@sha256:...`. An unqualified name resolves against Docker Hub. Give a bare reference, not a URI. The new VM boots a rootfs converted from that image rather than from an existing VM, so neither `source_vm_id` nor `source_vm_name` is given.

dockerfile.description: Dockerfile source. Accepted by the schema and ALWAYS REFUSED with a 400: the API does not build Dockerfiles, the SDKs do. Use arker.fork(dockerfile="./Dockerfile") from the Python or TypeScript SDK, or pass `image` to fork a prebuilt image here. COPY is why it works that way: it reads files on the caller's machine, and this field carries text while the caller waits for the fork response, so the server can never be handed those files. The field is kept rather than removed so this refusal can point at the SDK instead of answering with a bare `unknown field`.

nestedvirt.description: Request nested virtualization for a VM forked from `image`, including access to `/dev/kvm` inside the guest. Omit this field or pass `false` to disable it. The request returns 400 when the selected placement cannot provide nested virtualization.

source_org_id.description: Organization ID that owns `source_vm_name`. Supported for existing integrations and scheduled for removal in a later API version; use `source_org_name` for new integrations. Cannot be combined with `source_org_name`.

source_org_name.description: Organization name that owns `source_vm_name`. Currently accepts the caller's organization or `ArkerHQ`. Cannot be combined with `source_org_id`.

name.description: Optional name for the new VM, scoped to the caller's org.

description.description: Optional short description for the new VM. Blank strings normalize to null and forked VMs never inherit their source's description.

public.description: Make the new VM publicly forkable from other orgs.

ssh_public_keys.description: SSH public keys to authorize on the new VM as raw `authorized_keys` entries, such as `ssh-ed25519 AAAA... you@host`. The list becomes the VM's authorized-key set. Omit it or pass an empty list to create the VM with no keys; add keys later with `PATCH /v1/vms/{id}`. Configure inbound reachability through the VM's policy.

disk.description: Whether the new VM should include persistent disk storage.

durable.description: Whether the VM should preserve recoverable state across compute interruptions.

platforms.description: Preferred compute platforms for a public template, such as `["graviton3"]`. Supply multiple values to allow any listed platform. Omit or pass an empty list for automatic selection. A fork of an existing VM inherits its source platform.

layers.description: State to inherit from the source VM. Omit this field or pass `["disk", "memory"]` for a warm fork that resumes the source's filesystem and running processes. Pass `["disk"]` for a filesystem-only fork that cold-boots without the source's running processes. The list must include `disk`; supported values are `disk` and `memory`.

queueing_timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds this request may wait for capacity before failing with `capacity_unavailable`. Omit this field or pass `0` to fail immediately when capacity is unavailable.

policies.description: Network policy stored and enforced before the new VM first runs. Omit it to inherit the source VM's policy. Providing a policy replaces the inherited policy; an empty document selects the default posture of allow-all outbound traffic and authenticated inbound traffic. A non-empty document denies unmatched outbound traffic, so include outbound rules needed during setup. Network topology is inherited from the source. Set SSH keys through `ssh_public_keys`.

resources.description: Resource shape for the new VM.

registry_auth.description: Optional credentials for `image`. Ignored when forking from a source VM, which has no registry to authenticate against.

session_idx.description: Zero-based session index within the VM. Index 0 is the default shell a `/run` targets when it specifies neither `session_id` nor `session_idx`.

env.description: Optional environment-variable overrides for this session.

started_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp when execution or the session started.

source_org_id.description: Organization that owns the source VM.

region.description: Region containing the resource or activity.

provider.description: Public provider containing the session's VM.

next_cursor.description: Cursor for the next page, or null when no further page is available.

created_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp when the resource was created.

description.description: Short optional description owned by this VM.

hostname.description: Nullable base `.app` hostname for inbound services. The bare hostname selects guest port 8080. For another port, insert `-<port>` before the first dot: `<vm>-<port>.<provider>-<region>.arker.app`. Clients must not require this field to be present.

public.description: When `true`, other orgs can fork this VM (but cannot run on it).

root_source_vm_id.description: ID of the root (deepest-ancestor) source VM, if this VM was created by a chain of forks. None for VMs forked directly from an image.

root_source_vm_name.description: Name of the root source VM. Populated together with `root_source_vm_id`.

region.description: Customer-facing service region containing the VM.

last_active_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp of the machine's most recent activity — a run, an SSH session, an open tunnel, a resume, or being used as the source of a fork. Recorded when a stretch of activity begins and refreshed at most once a minute while it continues, so it is a recent-activity marker rather than a precise heartbeat. Null if the machine has not been active since it was created.

network.description: The VM's network object — SSH keys only. Inbound reachability and per-port exposure are derived from `policies`, not from this object.

max_vcpus.description: Hard vCPU ceiling for a fork of this VM. Requesting more fails the run.

min_vcpus.description: Smallest vCPU count accepted for this VM.

max_memory_mib.description: Hard memory ceiling (MiB) a fork can hotplug up to.

gpu_platforms.description: GPU sizing bounds for each GPU platform this VM can be forked onto; absent when it has no GPU platform. A base VM is GPU-agnostic and may be offered on several GPUs at once, so this is a list — clients pick the entry matching the platform they intend to request.

min_disk_mib.description: Smallest disk size (MiB) accepted for this VM. `0` means nodisk.

max_disk_mib.description: Largest disk size (MiB) accepted for this VM. `0` means nodisk.

platform.description: Immutable platform identity of this concrete VM.

compatible_platforms.description: Source-compatible platforms structurally offered in this region. This is not a live-capacity signal.

vms.description: VMs visible to the authenticated caller.

next_cursor.description: Cursor for the next page, or null when no further page is available.

deleted.description: True when the resource has been deleted.
True when the resource has been deleted.

cols.description: New terminal width in columns. Provide together with rows.

rows.description: New terminal height in rows. Provide together with cols.

timeout_secs.description: Idle auto-cancel window for the PTY; applies on the next attach.

session_id.description: The session to run in. Arker's run interface works like a terminal: sessions are tabs, each keeps its own state — working directory, environment, shell history — and each handles one run at a time. Create a session with `POST /v1/vms/{id}/sessions`, which also sets its starting directory and environment, then pass its id here. Run sequential commands in one session; for a long-running task, use `time_to_background: 0` in a session of its own so later work does not interrupt it. Distinct sessions run concurrently. A session that no longer exists is a 404. Omitted, the run uses the VM's default session, which every caller that omits it shares.

session_idx.description: Numeric session selector. `session_id` takes precedence when both selectors are sent.

command.description: Command submitted for execution. Omit it only for a signal request.

timeout.description: Maximum command runtime in seconds. Omitted means no limit; the run is killed only if you set a `timeout`. `0` is an explicit spelling of the same thing. This is separate from `time_to_background`, which controls how long the request waits for completion. A run is not complete until everything it spawned has exited, so this is also the bound on a run that leaves a daemon behind; when it fires, the run's processes are killed.

time_to_background.description: Sync window in seconds. `0` returns a pollable command run immediately after successful dispatch without polling for completion. A positive value bounds the synchronous wait. Omission uses the 300-second default. Control requests do not accept this field. This does not bound command execution; use `timeout` for the execution and kill bound. Values above approximately 350 seconds can exceed the load balancer idle limit.

background.description: Alias for `time_to_background`. `true` is exactly `time_to_background: 0` (return a pollable run immediately); `false` leaves the default sync window. Send only one of the two — supplying both is rejected, because they can disagree. Prefer `time_to_background`, which can also bound the wait instead of only switching it off.

queueing_timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds this request may wait to start before failing with `unavailable`. Omit this field or pass `0` to fail immediately when the run cannot start. This is independent of `timeout` and `time_to_background`.

end_symbol.description: Output marker used to determine when interactive execution is complete.

vcpu_count.description: Virtual CPU allocation for this run.

memory_backend.description: Preferred guest-memory mode when this run restores the VM. `file` maps the memory image from the host page cache; `uffd` supplies pages on demand. Omit this field to let the service choose. The setting has no effect when the VM is already running, and the response reports the mode used.

signal.description: Deliver a signal to the selected persistent session's foreground process group. When set, the service does not execute `command`; it returns a completed acknowledgement with no run id. Use `session_id` or `session_idx` to select the session.

policies.description: Complete network policy replacement applied to the VM before this run and retained afterward. A non-empty document replaces the persisted policy; an empty document selects the default posture of allow-all outbound traffic and authenticated inbound traffic. Omit it to use the current policy unchanged. If the policy cannot be stored and applied, the command does not run.

session_id.description: Session used by this run. Use this identifier to inspect or stop work that continues after the initial response. Absent for resource and signal requests that execute no command.

run_id.description: The run's own id. Present for executed runs; absent for operation acks (signal) with no run record.

state.description: Lifecycle state — "completed" for this shape. Read this (not the variant) for completion, uniformly with the run-status (`Run`) shape.

stdout.description: Standard output produced by the command.

stdout_encoding.description: Encoding used for stdout. Valid UTF-8 is returned directly; arbitrary bytes are base64 encoded.

stderr.description: Standard error produced by the command.

stderr_encoding.description: Encoding used for stderr. Valid UTF-8 is returned directly; arbitrary bytes are base64 encoded.

exit_code.description: The command's exit status. `null` means a prompt ended the run before a command completion marker was received, so no exit status is available. This is expected for `end_symbol` and REPL commands. If it is unexpected, `stdout` can show that an interpreter from an earlier run received the command. Exit the interpreter, pass `end_symbol: "none"`, or use another session.

dispatch.description: Execution mode selected by the service, when reported.

memory_requested_mib.description: Requested total memory in MiB when this run included a memory override. Absent when no override was requested.

memory_achieved_mib.description: Achieved total memory in MiB after applying the run's memory override. A memory reduction is best-effort, so this value can exceed `memory_requested_mib` when guest pages cannot be released. Absent when no override was requested.

memory_partial.description: True when a requested memory reduction was only partially applied. The command runs with the achieved allocation, and `memory_achieved_mib` reports that allocation. Defaults to false.

memory_backend.description: Which guest-memory mode this VM is restored with: `file` maps the memory image from the host page cache, `uffd` supplies pages on demand through a userfaultfd handler. Absent when this run involved no Firecracker restore — a `brush` dispatch, or a VM that was already running. Informational only: the mode is chosen per restore from the image's resident size, and an image reconstructed from object storage always uses `uffd`, which is a correctness requirement rather than a tuning choice.

completed_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp when execution reached a terminal state.

fail_reason.description: Client-safe platform failure explanation when `state` is `failed`. Distinct from `stderr`, which is the program's own error output. Null for runs that ran to completion.

`attaching` — the mount is pending. A stopped VM remains in this state until it resumes.

`mounted` — the filesystem is available in the VM.

`failed` — the VM cannot mount the filesystem. `status_detail` explains the cause. Transient errors remain in `attaching` while the service retries them.

gpu_sms.description: Number of GPU streaming multiprocessors available to the VM on EACH of its GPUs (a per-GPU value, uniform across the VM's devices; see `gpu_count`). Reported on GPU platforms such as `x86_64-l40s`. Response-only: a fork sizes GPU with `vgpu`.

gpu_vram_mib.description: GPU memory available to the VM, in MiB, on EACH of its GPUs (a per-GPU value; see `gpu_count`). Reported on GPU platforms. Response-only: a fork sizes GPU with `vgpu`.

gpu_count.description: Number of physical GPUs attached to the VM. `gpu_sms`/`gpu_vram_mib` are per-GPU values applied uniformly to every attached device, so the VM's total GPU allocation (and quota charge) is `gpu_count x per-GPU`. Reported on GPU platforms; absent means 1. Response-only: a fork sizes GPU with `vgpu`, which allocates at most one card.

VmResources.description: Resources a VM actually holds. GPU values are per-GPU; see `gpu_count` for the VM's total.

Vgpu.description: A slice of ONE physical GPU, in eighths of a card: 0.125 through 1. The constraints are the contract — an off-ladder fraction is rejected on the wire, not by the worker that later resolves it.

vgpu.description: Fraction of one physical GPU to allocate, in eighths of a card: 0.125, 0.25, 0.375, 0.5, 0.625, 0.75, 0.875, or 1. Resolved against the serving platform's GPU (`vgpu: 0.25` on `x86_64-l40s` is 35 SMs and 11517 MiB), so the same fraction is a different amount of silicon on a different card — see the per-platform table in the docs. Mutually exclusive with `gpu_sms` and `gpu_vram_mib`. Request-only: responses report the resolved `gpu_sms`/`gpu_vram_mib` and never this field.

ResourcesInput.description: Resource shape a caller asks for. GPU size is set with `vgpu`, in eighths of one card; the resolved per-GPU `gpu_sms`/`gpu_vram_mib` are reported back on the machine.

public_key.description: SSH public key in authorized_keys format.

fingerprint.description: Stable fingerprint of the SSH public key.

VmNetwork.description: SSH access configuration for a VM. Configure inbound application access through the VM's network policy.

ssh_public_keys.description: Authorized SSH keys with fingerprints. Returned by GET /v1/vms/{id}; omitted from list responses when empty.

description.description: Replace the VM description. Null or a blank string clears it; omit this field to leave it unchanged.

ssh_public_keys.description: Complete replacement for the VM's authorized SSH keys. Omit this field to leave the keys unchanged. Pass an empty array to remove all keys.

policies.description: Complete network policy replacement for the VM. A non-empty document replaces the persisted policy and applies it to the running VM. An empty document selects the default posture of allow-all outbound traffic and authenticated inbound traffic. Omit it to leave the current policy unchanged. If the policy cannot be stored and applied, the request fails.

CompatiblePlatform.description: One platform this source can be forked onto, with the resource limits that apply there. This is the authoritative per-platform record: when an entry carries bounds they win over the flat `min_*`/`max_*` fields on the VM, which are a single-platform convenience projection of the same data. CPU, memory, and disk limits come from the source VM; GPU limits come from the platform catalog.

id.description: Stable platform identifier used in fork requests.

min_vcpus.description: Smallest vCPU count accepted on this platform.

max_vcpus.description: Largest vCPU count accepted on this platform.

min_memory_mib.description: Smallest memory size accepted on this platform.

max_memory_mib.description: Largest memory size accepted on this platform.

min_disk_mib.description: Smallest disk size accepted on this platform.

max_disk_mib.description: Largest disk size accepted on this platform.

default_vcpus.description: vCPU count a fork that omits `resources.vcpu` receives on this platform.

default_memory_mib.description: Memory size in MiB a fork that omits `resources.memory_mib` receives on this platform.

default_disk_mib.description: Disk size in MiB a fork that omits `resources.disk_mib` receives on this platform. `0` means nodisk.

GpuResourceBand.description: A {min, max, default} band for one GPU resource on one platform. `default` is what a fork that omits the field receives.

max.description: Largest value accepted — the whole physical GPU. Requests above this return 400 rather than being clamped.

default.description: Value applied when the field is omitted on fork.

GpuPlatformLimits.description: GPU sizing bounds for one platform a VM can be forked onto.

platform.description: Platform label to request in `platforms` to land on this GPU, e.g. `x86_64-l40s`.

gpu.description: Human-readable GPU model for display, e.g. `NVIDIA L40S`. Never parse this for sizing — use the bands.

PlatformGpuLimits.description: GPU sizing bands for one compatible platform, from the platform catalog. Present on a `CompatiblePlatform` entry only when that platform has a GPU; absent means the platform has none. Bands are per GPU.

name.description: Human-readable GPU model for display, e.g. `NVIDIA L40S`. Never parse this for sizing — use the bands.

RegistryAuth.description:
Credentials for pulling `image` from a private registry. Used only for this one pull and never stored. Redacted from logs and telemetry.

For AWS ECR use username `AWS` with the output of `aws ecr get-login-password`; for Google Artifact Registry use `oauth2accesstoken` with an access token; for Docker Hub or GHCR use your username and a personal access token. Short-lived tokens are fine — the pull happens once, at fork time.

password.description: Registry password or token. Write-only: never returned by any endpoint and redacted wherever the request body is logged.
